Passing the **NCLEX (National Council Licensure Examination)** requires a structured study plan, discipline, and smart test-taking strategies. Below is a **comprehensive NCLEX to-do list** to help you prepare effectively.

---

### **📌 NCLEX Prep To-Do List**
*(Check off tasks as you complete them!)*

#### **📅 1. Understand the NCLEX Format & Requirements**
✅ **Register for the NCLEX** (via [Pearson VUE](https://www.pearsonvue.com/nclex/))
✅ **Check eligibility** (confirm with your state board of nursing)
✅ **Know the exam structure**:
   - **Computerized Adaptive Test (CAT)** – adjusts difficulty based on your answers
   - **75–265 questions** (max 6 hours, including breaks)
   - **8 major content areas** (Safe & Effective Care Environment, Health Promotion, Psychosocial Integrity, Physiological Integrity, etc.)
✅ **Understand passing standard** (not a percentage—based on ability estimation)

#### **📚 2. Gather Study Materials**
✅ **Choose a high-quality NCLEX review book** (e.g., *Saunders Comprehensive Review, UWorld, Hurst Review, Kaplan*)
✅ **Use an NCLEX question bank** (UWorld, Kaplan, BoardVitals, or NurseAchieve)
✅ **Watch video lectures** (Simple Nursing, Mark Klimek, Level Up RN, or NRSNG)
✅ **Get flashcards** (Anki, Picmonic, or self-made for meds, labs, and diseases)
✅ **Use mnemonics & memory tricks** (for pharmacology, prioritization, and delegation)

#### **📝 3. Create a Study Plan (6–12 Weeks Recommended)**
✅ **Assess your weak areas** (take a **diagnostic test** first)
✅ **Set a study schedule** (e.g., 4–6 hours/day, 5–6 days/week)
✅ **Break down topics by week** (e.g., Week 1: Fundamentals, Week 2: Pharm, Week 3: Med-Surg, etc.)
✅ **Mix content review + practice questions** (aim for **75–100 questions/day**)
✅ **Simulate test conditions** (timed, no distractions)

#### **🧠 4. Master NCLEX-Style Questions & Strategies**
✅ **Learn the 5 NCLEX question types**:
   - Multiple Choice
   - Select All That Apply (SATA)
   - Hot Spot
   - Drag-and-Drop
   - Fill-in-the-Blank
✅ **Practice prioritization & delegation** (Maslow’s Hierarchy, ABCs, safety first)
✅ **Understand "distractors"** (wrong answers that seem correct)
✅ **Use the "cover the answers" trick** (read the question first, then options)
✅ **Flag & review difficult questions** (UWorld/Kaplan explanations are gold!)

#### **💊 5. Focus on High-Yield Topics**
✅ **Pharmacology** (side effects, interactions, patient teaching)
✅ **Lab Values** (normal ranges & critical values)
✅ **Diseases & Disorders** (signs/symptoms, treatments, complications)
✅ **Fundamentals** (infection control, safety, legal/ethical issues)
✅ **Maternity & Pediatrics** (growth & development, labor stages, newborn care)
✅ **Mental Health** (therapeutic communication, crisis intervention)
✅ **Delegation & Leadership** (RN vs. LPN vs. CNA roles)

#### **⏳ 6. Time Management & Test-Taking Tips**
✅ **Pace yourself** (~1–2 min per question)
✅ **Skip & return to hard questions** (don’t dwell too long)
✅ **Eliminate wrong answers first** (narrow down choices)
✅ **Trust your gut** (your first instinct is often right)
✅ **Stay calm if the test shuts off at 75** (could mean you passed!)

#### **🧘 7. Mental & Physical Prep**
✅ **Get enough sleep** (7–9 hours/night, especially before test day)
✅ **Exercise & eat healthy** (boosts brain function)
✅ **Practice relaxation techniques** (deep breathing, meditation)
✅ **Avoid burnout** (take 1–2 rest days per week)
✅ **Stay positive** (visualize passing!)

#### **📅 8. Final Week Before the NCLEX**
✅ **Review marked/incorrect questions** (focus on weak areas)
✅ **Revisit key mnemonics & charts** (lab values, meds, etc.)
✅ **Take 1–2 full-length practice tests** (simulate real exam conditions)
✅ **Pack for test day**:
   - **ATI (Authorization to Test) email**
   - **Valid ID (passport or driver’s license)**
   - **Comfortable clothes & layers** (testing centers can be cold)
   - **Snacks & water** (for breaks)
   - **Earplugs (if sensitive to noise)**
✅ **Plan your route** (arrive 30–60 mins early)

#### **🎯 9. Test Day Strategy**
✅ **Stay calm & confident** (you’ve prepared for this!)
✅ **Read questions carefully** (watch for "most important," "first," "best")
✅ **Manage time wisely** (don’t rush, but don’t overthink)
✅ **Take breaks if needed** (optional 10-min breaks after 2 & 3.5 hours)
✅ **Don’t panic if the test is hard** (NCLEX adapts to your level)

#### **🎉 10. After the Test**
✅ **Avoid the "PVT trick"** (it’s not official—wait for results)
✅ **Check your state board’s website** (results usually in 2–6 weeks)
✅ **Celebrate your hard work!** (You did it! 🎉)

---
### **🔥 Bonus: Quick NCLEX Tips**
✔ **"Safety first!"** (Always pick the answer that protects the patient.)
✔ **"ABCs" (Airway, Breathing, Circulation)** – Prioritize life-threatening issues.
✔ **"Maslow before meds"** (Physiological needs > safety > love/belonging > esteem > self-actualization).
✔ **"If you see a lab value, assume it’s abnormal unless stated otherwise."**
✔ **"Delegation rule": RN assesses & evaluates; LPN/CNA can implement stable tasks.**

---
### **📌 Final Reminder:**
The NCLEX is **not about memorization**—it’s about **critical thinking, prioritization, and patient safety**. Stay consistent, trust your training, and you **WILL** pass!

**Good luck, future RN!** 🩺💙
